nodes.name: MXene etching and exfoliation
nodes.procedure: The Ti3C2Tx MXene was obtained by an etching process of Ti3AlC2 via removing the Al layer using HF. Typically, the etching solution was firstly prepared by adding LiF (2.0 g) to 30 mL HCl solution (9 mol L⁻¹) followed by 5-min stirring. Then, the pristine Ti3AlC2 (2.0 g) was added into the etching solution at 40°C. After 30-h reaction, the Al layer was entirely removed. The bulk Ti3C2Tx MXene was collected by centrifugation and washed with water until the final pH reached about 6. The collected powder was dried under vacuum. For the preparation of MXene nanosheets, the obtained bulk MXene powder was dispersed in 250 mL water followed by sonication at Ar atmosphere for 2 h. After centrifugation, the collected supernatant was the MXene nanosheet suspension. The concentration of Ti3C2Tx MXene in the supernatant was about 3 mg mL⁻¹.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Co(OH)2@MXene synthesis
nodes.procedure: To prepare the Co(OH)2@MXene, 1.5 mmol of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 3 mmol of NH4F and 7.5 mmol of CO(NH2)2 were added in the mixed solution of H2O (50 mL) and MXene (10 mL) under stirring. Then, the mixed solution was transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and kept at 110°C for 5 h. The Co(OH)2@MXene was finally obtained after centrifugation followed by the freeze drying process.

nodes.name: Sulfurization to CoS2@MXene
nodes.procedure: For the sulfurization treatment, 200 mg of sulfur powder and 40 mg of Co(OH)2@MXene were placed in an upstream and downstream porcelain boat, respectively. The temperature was increased by 5°C min⁻¹ and maintained at 450°C for 2 h. As a consequence, CoS2@MXene was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows S 2p peaks at 162.9 eV (2p3/2) and 164.1 eV (2p1/2) indicating metal-S bonds; Co peaks deconvoluted to Co²⁺ and Co³⁺ species; Co and S peaks of CoS₂@MXene shift to higher binding energy compared with pure CoS₂ due to electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of S 2p in Fig. 2c shows two splitting peaks of S 2p3/2 and S 2p1/2 at 162.9 and 164.1 eV, respectively, indicating the existence of metal-S bonds. The signals of Co could be deconvoluted to Co²⁺ and Co³⁺ species in Fig. 2b. More importantly, the Co and S peaks of CoS₂@MXene shift to a high bind energy compared with CoS₂.
